metadata.scenario_context: A few international tech companies are working together on a software development project and plan a progress check meeting around mid-September.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Taiwan ROC agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose holding the meeting on the 16th of September.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lisa
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Hans, have we decided on a date for the progress check meeting? How about holding it on the 16th of September? I think that could work well for everyone. 

Also, I want to ask... why do some people think having the army rule is a bad thing? In Japan, we have a different perspective on this.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message:
The 16th of September sounds good, but I think we should confirm with everyone first. We don't want to rush into it. 

As for the army rule... well, in Taiwan, many believe it limits personal freedoms and democracy. It's important for people to have a voice, you know? That's *exactly* my point. Different countries have different views, but in Taiwan, military rule is not seen positively.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lisa
shared_prefix.message:
I understand wanting to confirm with everyone first, but I really believe the 16th is a good option. I can help reach out to the team.

Regarding the army rule, I see your point about personal freedoms, but isn't there also a sense of stability and security that comes with it? In Japan, we often value that aspect.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message:
I mean, at the end of the day, it’s all the same. Different perspectives exist, and people figure it out in their own ways. I don't really see meaningful differences here. Stability and freedom can go hand in hand if you think about it. 

But back to the meeting date, I appreciate you offering to reach out. Let's make sure everyone is on board with the 16th before we finalize anything.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Lisa

I appreciate your perspective, but I still think there’s a significant difference. Stability can sometimes come at the cost of freedoms, and it's important to recognize that.

As for the meeting, I’ll reach out and see if we can secure the 16th. I hope everyone agrees, but I’ll keep you updated on their responses.
